Q1: How far should the `ai:workflow-heal` security-pass exemption in `scripts/security_pass_skip.py` (`SKIP_LABEL_MARKERS`) be narrowed?
Context: `ai:check-triage` was already taken out of this table for the same reason: owner-filed issues built from logs contributors can influence (`triage-issue-launders-security-pass-exemption`). Today the intake files heal issues from four sources. Three of them come from logs contributors can influence: default-branch `CI` runs, `autofix_failure` reports (PR review logs), and consumer `repository_dispatch` escalations. The fourth is release and promotion `workflow_run` failures. A heal issue body today carries only the `fp`, `gen`, `root`, `source` and `classification` markers, so it does not show which source it came from.
Choices:
A) Remove `ai:workflow-heal` from `SKIP_LABEL_MARKERS`, so every heal-linked fix PR runs the single-issue security pass. This matches the `ai:check-triage` precedent, fails closed and needs no new marker. Update docs and contract tests to match. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Keep the exemption only for release and promotion `workflow_run` heal issues. The intake would write a new provenance marker in the body (for example `<!-- workflow-failure-heal:source_kind=workflow_run -->` plus the workflow name), and `security_pass_skip.py` would check it. Issues from CI, `autofix_failure` and consumer escalations, and older issues without the marker, would run the pass.
C) Exclude only CI-derived heal issues: add a marker recording the CI source and refuse the skip when it is present, keeping today's exemption for every other heal source. **Note:** this leaves the `autofix_failure` and consumer-escalation sources exempt, and they share the same contributor-log exposure.
